title: Offbeat Kashmir in 12 Days: Gulmarg, Doodhpathri, Pahalgam, Daksum and the Gurez Valley
meta_title: Offbeat Kashmir Tour 12 Days with Gurez & Daksum
meta_description: 12-day Kashmir itinerary beyond the usual: Gulmarg Gondola, Doodhpathri meadows, Pahalgam, Daksum and Sinthan Top, a Dal Lake shikara and the Gurez Valley.
tagline: Meadows, high passes and the hidden Gurez valley on the Kishanganga
facts: Gulmarg, Doodhpathri, Pahalgam, Daksum, Srinagar, Gurez
Gondola Phase 2 about 3,950 m; Razdan Pass about 3,300 m
Private car; local cabs where required
intro: This plan goes beyond the classic Srinagar-Gulmarg-Pahalgam loop. After Gulmarg's gondola you stay in the quiet meadows of Doodhpathri, then in Pahalgam, and cross to the forested valley of Daksum for a day on Sinthan Top. After a night on Dal Lake you drive over Razdan Pass into Gurez, a valley of wooden villages on the Kishanganga that is cut off by snow for half the year. We tidied the original Day 6, which ran Pahalgam to Achabal to Daksum and back to Pahalgam: you now go one way, Pahalgam to Daksum via Achabal and Kokernag.
highlights: Gulmarg Gondola to Kongdoori and Apharwat
Doodhpathri's meadow and river, still uncrowded
Pahalgam, Betaab Valley, Aru and Chandanwari
Achabal and Kokernag Mughal-era springs on the way to Daksum
A day on Sinthan Top pass
Gurez Valley: Habba Khatoon peak, Dawar and the Kishanganga up to Chakwali

faqs.q: Is Kashmir safe to visit now?
faqs.a: The tourist areas on this route are heavily secured, and visitors continue to travel. After the April 2025 attack in Pahalgam some meadows were closed. We follow government advisories daily and change the plan if needed.
No. Gurez is open only to Indian citizens. Foreign guests can spend the extra days in Sonamarg instead.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay extra at Pahalgam and Gulmarg?
faqs.a: Yes. Local union cabs, pony rides and the Gondola are paid directly. We give you the official rate cards in advance.

faqs.q: Can I stay on a houseboat?
faqs.a: Yes. We recommend one night on a deluxe Dal Lake houseboat.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

price_note: Contact us for a personalised quote for your dates, flights and hotel choice.
entry_notes: Carry the original photo ID, not a photocopy. Security at airports and many temples checks it.
Phone and internet: Jio and Airtel work best across most of this route. Download offline Google Maps before hill or forest stretches, where signal drops.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Driving times
good_to_know.text: Indian roads are slower than the kilometres suggest: plan on 40 to 50 km an hour on highways and much less in hills and towns. Your driver's breaks and meal stops are built into the timings.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
